derived_reference_checks.interpretation: The standard-state reaction enthalpy is a thermodynamic lower-bound reference for the chemical reaction duty. The reported microwave energy is about 5.9 times this enthalpy. This ratio is not an efficiency: the reported process value has a source-specific meter boundary, and sensible heating, losses, plasma coupling, gas handling, separation and other loads are not reconciled here.

Only the charged alpha product's kinetic-energy component is directly accessible to an electrostatic charged-particle converter in the basic D-T reaction partition. The neutron component is neutral and must be treated as a separate blanket/thermal path unless a separately qualified neutral-particle conversion mechanism is specified. This arithmetic does not imply the alpha energy is captured by a converter: confinement, plasma heating, exhaust fraction, interception, conversion, conditioning and whole-plant parasitics remain separate.

Using the paper's rounded reported power values, suppressor-grid power is subtracted from gross recovered power. The derived net is 67 W and approximately 48.55% of 138 W, consistent with the paper's rounded 48% report. This is a check of the stated TMX test boundary, not a whole-plant or fusion-born energy efficiency.

This derives charged-product energy share from the source's simplified fuel-mixture model. It is not a direct-conversion efficiency, particle collection fraction, fusion gain or net plant electricity. The model's higher D-He3 temperature/density, side reactions and omitted stability/ignition physics remain separate constraints.

The three source-specific reciprocals are approximately 22.22 kWh/kg H2 at >99% conversion (45 g/kWh), 20.00 kWh/kg H2 at 92.4% conversion and 150 g/h (50 g/kWh), and 19.61 kWh/kg H2 at 76% conversion (51 g/kWh). The high-throughput point is not the >99% point, and the best energy-yield point is not the high-conversion point. These numbers retain the source's reported energy basis and are not assumed to be complete wall-plug-to-purified-H2 performance.

This is arithmetic over two different published source metrics, not a matched performance comparison. The gas-liquid tandem paper reports 1,161 kWh/kg NH3 (~0.861 g/kWh), while a separate 2026 integrated SOEC-HB plant model reports 8.14 kWh/kg NH3 (~122.85 g/kWh), a nominal 142.6x source-metric gap. Their boundaries and product contracts must be reconstructed before claiming a head-to-head gap. Separately, the JACS 2026 area rate of 7.7 nmol/s/cm2 corresponds to approximately 0.1133 kg NH3/m2/day, implying roughly 8,826 m2 active area per tonne/day at that rate. This geometric extrapolation is arithmetic only, not a scalability prediction; it omits packing, current distribution, mass transfer, degradation and balance-of-plant.

benchmark_targets.rationale: The 2026 source reports >99% conversion at 45 g/kWh, 92.4% conversion at 150 g/h and 50 g/kWh, and 76% conversion at 51 g/kWh. The stretch target requires these competing attributes to be reached together, rather than combining different operating points.

The combined stretch envelope challenges the 2026 review's separate shock-wave cost/conversion point and microwave conversion/selectivity point. It is a deliberate target for a new Pareto frontier, not a reported existing result.

The current review's 0.3–3 g NH3/kWh plasma range is not a matched full-chain comparison because hydrogen-production energy is omitted. The challenge is to reach at least 3 g accepted NH3/kWh after including H2 generation, plasma, electrolysis, gas handling and product separation, then compare with Haber-Bosch under the same boundary.

The 2026 300 MW plasma-biogas-reforming TEA reports about EUR 840/t syngas and about 44% plant efficiency, with modeled cases below EUR 600/t under favourable renewable-electricity assumptions. The stretch target requires the cost and plant-efficiency thresholds to hold together under the same matched service and full plant boundary.

The September 2026 microwave NH3 study identifies heat-balance losses and an insulating sleeve of cold NH3 as an improvement pathway. This target tests whether integrated thermal management can reduce net grid-to-accepted-H2 specific energy by at least 15% while retaining >99% conversion and at least 150 g/h in the same operating point. It is a stretch target; the cited 150 g/h paper point is 92.4% conversion, so all three target attributes must be demonstrated together rather than borrowed across source points.

Test the missing bridge in the 2026 plasma-electrocatalytic ammonia paper: whether a state-resolved N2(v) population generated upstream is actually delivered to the catalyst interface and causally contributes to isotope-attributed NH3 under matched controls. This is an evidence/causal qualification target, not a numerical performance result.

The 2026 gas-liquid plasma-electrocatalytic tandem source reports 1,161 kWh/kg NH3; a separate 2026 integrated SOEC-Haber-Bosch plant model reports 8.14 kWh/kg NH3 at plant boundary and 63% LHV efficiency. The plasma route is currently far from this benchmark on its reported energy metric. The challenge target is not merely to exceed the 3 g/kWh intermediate research threshold: it requires at least 10% lower energy than 8.14 kWh/kg (<=7.32 kWh/kg) at the same accepted NH3 specification and reconciled complete boundary. This target remains blocked until source system boundaries, including desalination, storage and product delivery exclusions, are normalized.

The November 2026 PPH study reports 95% conversion/100% selectivity on diluted CH4/He and a separate 27 kWh/kg H2 minimum energy under pure methane. This stretch target intentionally requires >=90% conversion, >=99% selectivity and <=25 kWh/kg accepted H2 at one matched feed/operating point, while including CO2-plasma regeneration and 100 reaction/regeneration cycles with >=90% productivity retention. No such combined point or durability is currently established.

The 2026 flexible Haber-Bosch model reports 10–120% load and 3%/min ramp; a separate year-long fatigue/scheduling model reports 10–100% load at 3%/min, and a three-level dispatch study reports >80% lower modeled reactor cycling. The plasma challenge must therefore match plant-level service across the same renewable profiles and fatigue boundaries before claiming flexibility advantage.

The published hybrid DBD model reports mean publication-grouped five-fold R2=0.441, best fold 0.791, worst fold 0.024, and prospective R2=0.92 on 10 new points within the explored domain. The Luminous challenge is to reproduce the exact 27-paper split, then target mean grouped R2>=0.55 and worst-fold R2>=0.15 with calibrated intervals and applicability reporting. The LOPO target is reported separately and is not directly equated with the five-fold score. A sealed prospective reactor holdout must include at least 20 independent points. The source's 358 abstract/methods versus 357 conclusion row-count discrepancy must be resolved against SI before any exact reproduction claim.

The target preserves the reported stoichiometric energy point separately from the H2-rich high-conversion point. A candidate must improve the accepted syngas Pareto frontier under a complete grid-side energy and product boundary; the source's 264/277 value discrepancy is a blocker until resolved.

The 2026 cyclic CRG paper demonstrates carbon formation/gasification but uses plasma-deposited power, has distinct modes, and reports only about 0.5 vol% maximum O2 after three passes. This target tests real carbon closure, durability and retained useful syngas over 100 cycles with full grid-side energy accounting.

The September 2026 QWCCR study reports 1.31 ms ACR response on a 160→180 W step and 1.10 ms on a 180→160 W step, with OES/high-speed imaging proxies; those are not accepted H2 product delivery response times. The waveguide MWPJ study reports a separate approximately sevenfold relative H2 production efficiency gain and approximately 47.5% critical NH3 fraction under its own Ar-diluted feed and flow architecture. The benchmark's paradigm shift is to measure command→plasma→diagnostic→gas composition→purified H2→customer delivery separately, then optimize full grid-to-accepted-H2 service under realistic load profiles. The 1 s customer-service settling target is an aspirational research target, not a source-reported or achieved result.

Compare plasma-catalytic dual-membrane experiments, catalytic membrane process models, electrochemical MEA operating modes, membrane-reactor surrogates and microwave plasma at one accepted H2 purity/pressure/service boundary and full grid-to-delivered-product energy. A hybrid plasma/catalyst/membrane/electrochemical topology is a falsifiable research hypothesis, not an achieved result.
